deals_cleared.merger_description: Hillhouse Investment Management, Ltd. (**Hillhouse**), through Atlas Investments Holdings Limited (**Atlas BidCo**), has agreed to indirectly acquire a minority stake in Dione Topco Ltd. (**Dione Topco**), pursuant to a Share Purchase Agreement dated 19 May 2026 (the **Acquisition**).

events.title: Notification waiver determination published
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Atlas Investments Holdings Limited (Atlas BidCo), which is indirectly
and wholly-owned by certain funds managed and/or advised by
Hillhouse Investment Management, Ltd. (Hillhouse) and its affiliates,
applied for a notification waiver in respect of its proposed
acquisition of a minority stake in Dione Topco Ltd. (Dione Topco), as
described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
18 July 2026

The acquirer, Hillhouse, is a global investment firm that primarily
invests in the fields of business services, healthcare, consumer,
education, and real assets sectors.
The target, Dione Topco, is the holding company for the indirectly
wholly owned group of companies comprising LRQA Group Limited
(LRQA, together with its subsidiaries, the LRQA Group). The LRQA
Group is a global provider of inspection and certification services to
both public and private sector customers with customers across a
range of industries, including energy and renewables, construction,
food and beverage, consumer goods manufacturing, and technology,
amongst others.
The LRQA Group is headquartered in Birmingham, United Kingdom,
and with offices across Europe, the Americas, Asia Pacific, and the
Middle East. The LRQA Group’s services can be divided into four
service areas: (a) assessment and certification services, (b)
inspection services, (c) data analytics and consulting services
(including environmental, social and governance (ESG)), and (d)
cybersecurity services.
One of Hillhouse’s portfolio companies, Ascentium, also offers ESG
consulting services.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is no overlap between Hillhouse (and its connected
entities) and LRQA Group in the supply of testing, inspection
and certification services in Australia
b. there is a small overlap between Hillhouse (and its
connected entities) and LRQA Group in the supply of ESG
consulting services in Australia
c. there are alternative suppliers of testing, inspection and
certification, and ESG consulting services in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.

AkzoNobel will be renamed, with the final name to be determined at a later stage.

events.title: AkzoNobel - Axalta - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Akzo Nobel N.V. (AkzoNobel)’s and Axalta Coating Systems Ltd.
(Axalta)’s proposed entry into a merger agreement (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, AkzoNobel, is a global paints and coatings
manufacturer headquartered in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.
AkzoNobel produces and markets paints and coatings, including
automotive and speciality coatings, powder coatings, industrial
coatings, and marine and protective coatings, for professional, do-it-
yourself, and industrial end users.
The target, Axalta, is a global coatings manufacturer and distributer
headquartered in Philadelphia, USA. Axalta supplies a range of
coating solutions, including vehicle refinish coatings for light
vehicles, commercial vehicles, electric motors, and building facades.

AkzoNobel and Axalta overlap in the supply of vehicle refinish and
powder coatings in Australia.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The market share aggregation in vehicle refinish products in
Australia as a result of the Acquisition is estimated to be low.
• In relation to the supply of powder coating products in Australia,
despite concerns raised in third-party feedback regarding
consolidation, Axalta is a relatively small competitor so there will
be a very small increase in the market share of the merged
entity, and the merged entity would continue to face competition
from other competitors.
• In relation to the supply of vehicle refinish in Australia, the
merged entity would continue to face competition from
alternative large, established suppliers, as well as many smaller
competitors.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

events.title: Amazon - Globalstar - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by a division of the Commission constituted by a direction issued pursuant to section 19 of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Amazon.com, Inc. (Amazon), via its wholly-owned subsidiary,
Grapefruit Acquisition Sub II, LLC, proposes to acquire Globalstar,
Inc (Globalstar), its subsidiaries, assets and facilities (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Amazon, supplies retail services, media content,
electronic devices and on-demand technology services (including
cloud computing). Amazon also operates Amazon Leo, which will
supply high-capacity broadband/fixed satellite service (FSS) to
government agencies, business and consumers using low Earth orbit
satellites. Amazon Leo plans to launch its commercial service in
mid-2026. In Australia, Amazon Leo has an agreement with NBN Co
to deliver fixed-satellite broadband services to customers in regional,
remote and rural Australia.
The target, Globalstar, supplies global narrowband/mobile satellite
service (MSS) connectivity services for voice and data
communications applications. Globalstar provides these services to
government agencies, businesses and consumers using allocated
MSS spectrum, including in Australia.
Globalstar currently provides Apple, Inc. with direct-to-device (D2D)
satellite connectivity services on certain iPhone and Apple Watch
models, allowing users to send and receive messages while outside
of cellular and Wi-Fi coverage (e.g. Australian users can currently
use this capability for emergency messaging, to request roadside
assistance, and to share their location). Amazon has signed an
agreement to continue providing Apple, Inc. with D2D services post-
acquisition.

Amazon and Globalstar (together, the Parties) both provide, or will
soon provide, satellite services. However, they hold spectrum
authorisations in different frequency bands and their offerings
appear to serve different use cases. In particular, Amazon Leo's
system will use FSS spectrum to provide high-capacity connectivity
services to specialised fixed terminals, while Globalstar uses MSS
spectrum to deliver low-capacity connectivity services directly to
individual consumer mobile handsets or devices.
The ACCC has not identified any non-horizontal relationships
between the Parties.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The Parties do not compete closely in the supply of satellite
services in Australia, as they hold spectrum authorisations in
different frequency bands and their offerings serve different use
cases.
• Post-Acquisition, the merged entity would continue to face
competition from several alternative suppliers of FSS and MSS
services, including other entities (such as SpaceX’s Starlink)
which supply both services.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

The target, ZIM, is a public company listed on the New York Stock
Exchange in the USA (NYSE: ZIM). Its headquarters are in Israel.
Globally, ZIM is active in container line shipping and related services,

ZIM operates a single container liner shipping service, which
connects Australian east coast ports (Brisbane, Sydney and
Melbourne) to ports in Asia (Busan, Qingdao, Shanghai, Ningbo,
Yantian).
ZIM also has a limited presence in the downstream freight
forwarding services market in Australia. HLAG does not conduct
these activities in Australia.

Horizontal overlap in the supply of container liner shipping services
between Asia and Australia.

and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in

regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering

and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The Parties’ are relatively small providers of container liner

standard hours (General Veterinary Services) in Adelaide. Small

animals (such as cattle, sheep and horses), and offer services such
as first opinion consultations, general and preventative health
care/advice, surgery, microchipping, dentistry, radiology, pathology,
pharmacy and related services such as puppy school.
While Paws supplies specialist ophthalmic veterinary services, CVS
Group does not supply these services in Adelaide, and therefore
there is no overlap between the Parties in relation to these services.

the information and documents that were submitted with the

• the market share aggregation resulting from the Acquisition is
estimated to be low;
• the merged entity would continue to face competition from
multiple alternative General Veterinary Services practices in the
local area surrounding Paws;
• the merged entity would continue to face competition from other
large suppliers of General Veterinary Services at the state and
national levels.

events.title: OpenAI-Ona - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by a division of the Commission constituted by a direction issued pursuant to section 19 of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
The proposed acquisition of 100% of the share capital of Gitpod, Inc.
(known as Ona) by OpenAI Group PBC, an entity controlled by the
OpenAI Foundation (OpenAI) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, OpenAI, develops artificial intelligence (AI) foundation
models, including its GPT family of models, as well as foundation
model-based services such as ChatGPT.
OpenAI also supplies Codex, an AI-powered agent designed to
enable software developers to perform and automate various
software engineering tasks, subject to human direction and review.
Codex is typically accessed through user-facing interfaces and
developer tools and is powered by OpenAI’s own foundation models.
The target, Ona, supplies a platform that enables enterprise
customers to deploy and orchestrate AI-powered agents to run
software engineering tasks within the customer’s own infrastructure
or cloud environment. These agents can run autonomously in the
background and at scale, including when individual developers are
not actively using their laptops. Ona’s platform works across
multiple cloud platforms and with multiple foundation models.

OpenAI and Ona (together, the Parties) overlap in the supply of AI
software development tools. However, their offerings address
different use cases. In particular, OpenAI’s Codex appears to be
primarily used interactively by developers to assist with discrete
coding tasks, while the Ona platform focuses on and enables
background execution of software engineering workflows within the
customer’s own infrastructure or cloud environment.
The Ona platform can integrate third-party foundation models,
including OpenAI’s GPT models.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• OpenAI and Ona do not appear to compete closely in the supply
of AI software development tools in Australia, given their
offerings address different use cases and Ona has a limited
presence in Australia.
• Post-Acquisition, the merged entity would likely continue to face
competition from multiple alternative suppliers of AI software
development tools, including both developer-facing coding
assistants and automation-focused solutions.
• Post-Acquisition, the merged entity would be unlikely to have an
ability and incentive to foreclose rival AI software development
product providers’ access to AI foundation models given there
are multiple alternative suppliers of AI foundation models.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.

The acquirer, Midea, is a major international technology group,
organised into several divisions, including Smart Home, Industrial
Technology, Building Technology, Robotics & Automation, New Energy,
Healthcare and Smart Logistics. Relevant to the Acquisition, through
its Smart Home division, Midea manufactures whitegoods and

appliances, laundry appliances, air purifiers, fans, and portable air
conditioning appliances.

appliances under its ‘Midea’ brand to retailers, as well as whitegoods
and electronic household appliances on a ‘white label’ basis to
wholesalers and a ‘private label’ basis to retailers.
The target, Residentia, is a private company, founded in 2014 and
headquartered in Melbourne, Australia. Residentia is active in the
distribution of whitegoods and electronic household appliances
across Australia and New Zealand. It supplies products under its own
brands (Esatto, InAlto, Omega and Sôlt) and some third-party brands
(Teka and Elica) to traditional retailers and commercial merchants.
Residentia also (to a very limited extent) supplies private label
whitegoods and electronic household appliances to retailers.

between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
There is an overlap between Midea and Residentia (the Parties) in the
supply of the following types of whitegoods and electronic household
appliances under the Parties’ and third party brands to retailers:
microwaves, range hoods, portable air conditioners, dishwashers,
built-in cooking hobs, dryers, ovens, refrigerators, washing machines,
air purifiers, and cooling fans.

label whitegoods and electronic household appliances to retailers.

electronic household appliances to Residentia.

as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the effect of
substantially lessening competition in any market. In reaching its
decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC makes the
following findings.
• The increase in concentration in relation to each of the types of
whitegoods and electronic household appliances supplied by the
Parties under their own and third-party brands would be small and

than its business of supplying Midea-branded products, Midea

customers could switch to alternative suppliers of white label
whitegoods and electronic household appliances.

to foreclose rival manufacturers’ access to wholesale distribution
channels because Residentia is only a small customer of branded
whitegoods and electronic household appliances in Australia and
it already sources the majority of its products from Midea.
